tours.title: How xpl links guides to source
tours.summary: xpl turns a repository and an authored explanation into an interactive code guide. xpl indexes source, checks that explanation links point to current code, and exports one HTML page. These checks cannot prove the prose is correct or complete. This tour shows the reader path and the four main parts behind it.

steps.note:
### A source-backed guide starts with code and an author

The guide author writes an explanation for the source repository. xpl checks its source links and exports an interactive guide. The guide reader moves between diagrams and code; the prose still needs human review.

### The CLI runs the authoring workflow

Commands load the index and guide, check an author's patch, and write or export the result. The command layer owns filesystem access.

### Shared rules check each source link

The core builds checked anchors from the index and source text. Its patch merge also preserves fields a reader edited.

### The index records what source contains

The indexer discovers files and extracts symbols and relationships. The guide can then refer to known locations rather than free-form line claims.

### The viewer lets readers follow both directions

The page renders a diagram and code together. Selecting a diagram element finds its source, while cursor movement can highlight related elements.
